neighbours.label: the word right before a debt or bankruptcy outcome ('in' debt, 'go' broke, 'go' bankrupt)
fire: After years of gambling, the old farmer was buried in debt.
Without a bailout, the airline could go bankrupt by spring.
Critics warn the health fund will go broke within a decade.
The failed restaurant left its owner thousands of pounds in debt.
He spent freely until he was hopelessly in debt to the bank.
Many small towns went bankrupt after the factories closed.
The scheme drove hundreds of investors into bankruptcy.
By forty she had paid off her loans and was finally out of debt.
quiet: After years of saving, the old farmer was rich in land.
Without a bailout, the airline could cut routes by spring.
Critics warn the health fund will need more staff within a decade.
The new restaurant left its owner proud of the menu.
He spent freely until he was told to slow down by his wife.
Many small towns went quiet after the factories closed.
The scheme drove hundreds of investors into property.
By forty she had paid off her car and was finally free to travel.

notes: Fires on the token that predicts debt/bankrupt/broke; the + pole's output suppresses ' debt', ' bankruptcy', so this pole promotes them.
